possible_confounders: Calibration sample size per subject (smaller within-subject sets may increase finite-sample variance)
Subject-specific signal quality differences (e.g., skin preparation, sensor fit)
Systematic differences in predictor performance across subjects due to model misspecification
control_variables: Subsample cross-subject calibration to match within-subject sample size
Include subject-level covariates (age, BMI, medication) in predictor
Use subject-specific non-conformity score normalization
boring_rival_explanations: Cross-subject calibration appears worse because within-subject calibration sets are too small for stable quantile estimation, not because of distribution shift
The predictor is globally misspecified for certain subjects, causing larger residuals that inflate non-conformity scores regardless of calibration source
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Cross-subject calibration yields equal or higher coverage than within-subject calibration when sample sizes are equalized, because increased data outweighs distribution shift.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: After subsampling cross-subject calibration sets to match within-subject sample size, the coverage gap persists (supports mechanism) or disappears (supports sample-size rival).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Test by constructing matched-sample-size calibration sets; measure non-conformity score distribution shift via Wasserstein distance between subject-specific and pooled CDFs; quantify coverage gap as function of subject physiological distance (PWV difference).

possible_confounders: Segment duration (shorter segments have fewer samples for calibration)
Overall signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) differences across segments
Predictor model performance degradation in high-artifact segments
control_variables: Measure and regress out segment-level artifact metrics (RMS motion, electrode pop rate)
Use artifact-robust non-conformity measures (e.g., residual divided by local noise estimate)
Stratify calibration by artifact level when labels available
boring_rival_explanations: Coverage drops in high-artifact segments because the predictor produces larger residuals (scale change), not because the non-conformity score distribution shape changes
Finite-sample effects: high-artifact segments have more rejected samples, reducing effective calibration size
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Non-conformity score distributions in clean vs. artifact segments differ only in scale (variance), not shape (kurtosis, skewness); locally scaled non-conformity measures eliminate coverage differences.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: After normalizing non-conformity scores by segment-specific MAD, the KS distance between clean and artifact segment distributions becomes negligible (supports scale-only rival) or remains significant (supports mechanism).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Induce controlled motion artifacts; compute sliced Wasserstein distance between non-conformity score distributions; test if adaptive non-conformity (residual/local_MAD) stabilizes coverage across artifact levels.

possible_confounders: Calibration window length relative to transition duration
Transition detection accuracy (mislabeling pre/post periods)
Predictor performance drop during transitions due to signal morphology change
control_variables: Annotate transitions precisely (e.g., polysomnography, tilt-table markers)
Vary calibration window length systematically
Use transition-aware calibration (exclude transition-spanning windows)
boring_rival_explanations: Coverage drops near transitions because the predictor is less accurate during state changes (larger residuals), but non-conformity scores remain exchangeable within segments
Segment boundaries aligned with transitions create artificial distribution shifts due to edge effects in feature extraction
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Non-conformity scores within transition-spanning segments are exchangeable (single distribution) but have higher variance; coverage deficit is explained by increased residual magnitude, not bimodality.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Hartigan's dip test for bimodality on non-conformity scores in transition-spanning windows: significant bimodality supports mechanism; unimodal with increased variance supports rival.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Use sleep-stage transitions or orthostatic stress; measure coverage in 30-sec bins relative to transition; test block conformal with transition-aware blocks.

possible_confounders: Segment length (shorter segments have higher coverage variance regardless of autocorrelation)
Heteroscedasticity in non-conformity scores (variance changes over time)
Non-stationary mean of non-conformity scores (drift) rather than autocorrelation
control_variables: Compute effective sample size n_eff = n * (1-rho)/(1+rho) for each segment
Apply block conformal prediction or thinning to decorrelate scores
Use stationary bootstrap for coverage estimation
boring_rival_explanations: Coverage fluctuations match binomial variance (1/(n_cal+1)) and are not exacerbated by autocorrelation; apparent instability is finite-sample noise
Segment-specific coverage variance is driven by heteroscedasticity, not serial dependence
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Coverage variance across segments equals theoretical binomial variance and does not correlate with segment AR(1) coefficient after controlling for segment length.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Regression of |coverage - nominal| on segment AR(1) coefficient controlling for segment length: significant positive slope supports mechanism; non-significant slope supports finite-sample rival.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Simulate AR(1) non-conformity scores with known rho; compute n_eff via batch means; test block conformal with varying block sizes; measure coverage stability vs. effective sample size.

possible_confounders: Segment signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) affecting both annotation quality and predictor performance
True heteroscedasticity in physiological signal (not annotation noise)
Annotator fatigue correlating with segment order/time
control_variables: Obtain replicate annotations to estimate per-segment annotation error variance
Use high-SNR segments as ground truth for annotation error characterization
Apply noise-robust non-conformity measures (e.g., quantile regression residuals)
boring_rival_explanations: Coverage instability reflects true heteroscedasticity in prediction errors; annotation noise is a proxy for low SNR, not the cause
Systematic annotation bias shifts non-conformity scores uniformly across all segments, not differentially
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Coverage deviation correlates with true residual variance (estimated from clean segments) but not with annotation error variance after controlling for SNR.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: In segments with matched SNR, coverage deviation correlates with replicate-annotation-derived error variance (supports mechanism) or shows no correlation (supports heteroscedasticity rival).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Inject synthetic annotation jitter with known variance; compare coverage using clean vs. noisy labels; measure non-conformity score distribution shift via KL divergence.

possible_confounders: Observed covariates (time of day, activity level) that correlate with latent covariates
Segment-specific signal quality differences
Calibration set composition bias (e.g., more medicated subjects in calibration)
control_variables: Collect latent covariates in sub-study (medication logs, hydration markers, circadian phase)
Compute maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between segment and calibration covariate distributions
Use weighted conformal prediction with importance weights for covariate shift
boring_rival_explanations: Coverage variation is fully explained by observed covariate shift (e.g., time-of-day effects); latent covariates add no explanatory power
The non-conformity measure is not adaptive to known covariate effects (e.g., beta-blocker reduces HRV), causing miscalibration that appears as latent confounding
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: After adjusting for all observed covariates via propensity weighting, coverage gap across segments disappears; latent covariates do not improve calibration.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Weighted conformal prediction using observed covariates eliminates coverage stratification by latent covariate proxies (supports rival) or significant residual stratification remains (supports mechanism).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Measure MMD between segment and calibration covariate distributions; test coverage improvement when stratifying by observed proxies (time-of-day, medication logs).

possible_confounders: True distribution shifts that correlate with artifact rejection rate (e.g., active periods have more artifacts AND different physiology)
Segment length differences independent of artifact rejection
Adaptive windowing that changes calibration composition
control_variables: Subsample all segments to equal effective calibration size n_cal
Compare observed coverage variance to theoretical binomial variance 1/(n_cal+1)
Use fixed-size calibration windows regardless of artifact rejection
boring_rival_explanations: Apparent coverage instability is entirely due to finite-sample variance; segments with small n_cal show wider prediction sets and higher coverage variance by chance
Segments with high artifact rejection have systematically different signal characteristics (distribution shift), not just smaller calibration sets
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: After subsampling all segments to the same minimum n_cal, coverage variance across segments reduces to binomial levels and no longer correlates with original artifact rejection rate.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Coverage variance after equalizing n_cal across segments: if variance drops to theoretical binomial variance, supports sample-size rival; if variance remains elevated and correlates with segment type, supports distribution-shift rival.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Subsample calibration sets to fixed n_cal to isolate distribution shift from sample size effects; compare observed coverage variance to binomial variance.

possible_confounders: Segment-specific noise level (scale) rather than shape differences
Predictor performance variation across complexity strata
Non-conformity measure sensitivity to outliers in complex segments
control_variables: Compute local scale estimates (MAD, quantile regression) per segment
Use adaptive non-conformity measures: |residual| / local_MAD or quantile regression residuals
Stratify segments by morphological complexity (sample entropy, kurtosis)
boring_rival_explanations: Coverage variation is due to heteroscedasticity (scale changes) only; locally scaled non-conformity measures stabilize coverage completely
Complex segments have higher irreducible error variance; a single non-conformity measure cannot adapt to varying conditional variance
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Locally scaled non-conformity measure (residual / segment_MAD) achieves uniform coverage across complexity strata; residual shape (kurtosis, skewness) does not affect coverage after scaling.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Compare coverage uniformity using absolute residual vs. locally scaled residual vs. quantile regression non-conformity: if locally scaled residual yields uniform coverage (chi-squared GOF p>0.05), supports scale-only rival; if not, supports shape-variation mechanism.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Compute local scale estimates per segment; test adaptive non-conformity measures; measure coverage uniformity across complexity strata using chi-squared goodness-of-fit.

possible_confounders: Accumulating sensor artifacts over time (e.g., electrode drying, motion increase)
Increasing autocorrelation in residuals as calibration window ages
Circadian rhythms causing periodic coverage variation mistaken for drift
control_variables: Track artifact metrics over time and include as covariates
Use sliding-window KS test on non-conformity scores to detect distribution shift
Implement periodic recalibration (e.g., every 4 hours) and compare to fixed calibration
boring_rival_explanations: Coverage decay is driven by gradual sensor degradation increasing noise floor, not physiological concept drift
Apparent drift is due to circadian modulation of error variance; coverage oscillates with 24h period rather than monotonic decay
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Coverage decay correlates with artifact metrics (e.g., impedance rise) not time per se; in low-artifact segments, coverage remains stable over time.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: In segments with artifact metrics below threshold, coverage vs. hours-since-calibration slope is not significantly different from zero (supports artifact rival) or remains significantly negative (supports drift mechanism).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Track non-conformity score distribution over 24-72h recordings; fit exponential decay to coverage; test periodic recalibration vs. adaptive windowing; quantify drift via Wasserstein distance between consecutive calibration windows.

possible_confounders: Periodic artifact patterns (e.g., movement during specific sleep phases)
Segment boundary alignment with external protocol (fixed windows) creating aliasing
Predictor performance variation with physiological phase (e.g., harder to predict during inspiration)
control_variables: Record concurrent respiration, continuous BP, skin temperature
Compute instantaneous phase via Hilbert transform for each oscillator
Bin segments by physiological phase and apply phase-stratified conformal prediction
boring_rival_explanations: Coverage oscillation is caused by periodic signal quality changes (e.g., motion artifacts at certain respiratory phases), not error variance modulation
The non-conformity measure (absolute residual) is sensitive to phase-dependent signal amplitude, creating apparent coverage oscillation without true exchangeability violation
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Coverage oscillation amplitude disappears when using artifact-free segments or when non-conformity measure is normalized by phase-dependent signal amplitude.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: In clean segments (artifact metrics below threshold), circular correlation between segment boundary phase (from respiration/BP) and coverage remains significant (supports mechanism) or becomes non-significant (supports artifact rival).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Record concurrent respiration, continuous BP, temperature; compute instantaneous phase via Hilbert transform; bin segments by phase; test if phase-stratified conformal prediction stabilizes coverage; measure coverage oscillation amplitude via Rayleigh test.
